A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BadSFL and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, and references. V1's appendix Scaffold algorithm and Neurotoxin illustration are retained in v3's main text, allowing comparison without treating their relocation as deletion.

before.justification: V1 reports original GAN supplementation, attack accuracy, persistence, and defense experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 in Figures 5-8.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and reports additional attack comparisons and defense evaluations in Figures 6-8.

M1.justification: V1 Algorithm 1 and v3 Algorithm 2 specify the same BadSFL procedure. GAN supplementation, trigger injection, the future-model objective in Equations 1-3, and the control-variate update are unchanged; the new benign-client narrative does not introduce an algorithmic step.

E1.justification: The three datasets and the label-flipping, pattern-trigger, and feature-trigger tasks are retained. However, the settings and Figure 7b change 'Red Car' to 'Race Car' while retaining closely matching existing trajectories. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects a label or changes the evaluated image subset.

E2.justification: V3 adds Irreversible Backdoor Attack (IBA) and 3DFed alongside Black-box and Neurotoxin. Their curves appear throughout Figures 6-8, substantially expanding the actual comparison set beyond v1's two baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1, the 100 communication rounds, client sampling, data partitioning, and principal training settings remain unchanged. The reported defense configurations change: v1 describes differential privacy, pruning, and anomaly detection together, whereas v3 Figure 8 identifies differential privacy plus pruning and separate FLAME and SparseFed conditions. This establishes revised reported settings, not that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 substantially broadens defense robustness testing through separate CIFAR-100 feature-trigger evaluations against FLAME and SparseFed in Figure 8e-f. These examine persistence under additional defenses. The GAN supplementation analysis and discussion of Neurotoxin's unexpected behavior are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands for the experimental curves. The additional results use the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 6-8 add IBA and 3DFed results, and Figure 8 adds FLAME and SparseFed outcomes. Existing reported rankings also change: in Figure 6e, BadSFL and Black-box end near 50% and 100% respectively in v1, but near 100% and 50% in v3. This is an unexplained revision of reported results, not an established methodological performance gain. Figure 5's results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1-3 and the formal Scaffold update rules are retained. Moving Scaffold's pseudocode from the appendix into the main text adds no mathematical result, and neither version supplies a new theorem, proof, or derivation establishing benign-client amplification.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes predicting global-model convergence to preserve backdoors. V3's title, abstract, and introduction elevate control-variate tampering that recruits benign clients into the central contribution and assert greater vulnerability than FedAvg. The established first-Scaffold-attack and persistence claims remain, while the simultaneous-defense claim increases from three defenses to four.

C2.justification: V3 adds a substantive causal interpretation: Scaffold's correction mechanism steers honest clients toward poisoned updates and amplifies the attack. V1 instead explains control variates primarily as a reference for aligning the poisoned model with future global updates. No new mechanism-isolating experiment accompanies this interpretation; the existing Neurotoxin uncertainty remains.

D1.justification: V3's Figure 8 captions explicitly associate panels with particular defense conditions, improving the documentation of those results. Hardware, GAN architecture details, optimizers, and Table 1 hyperparameters remain unchanged, and no code-access or additional baseline implementation information is supplied.

R1.justification: The central positioning shifts from overcoming Scaffold's resistance to existing backdoors toward exposing a security cost of its correction mechanism relative to FedAvg. V3 also expands prior-attack discussion and adds references including IBA, 3DFed, A3FL, and SparseFed, while removing BadNets and FLTrust.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and substantial portions of the introduction are rewritten. V3 introduces numbered sections and subsections, expands the research-gap discussion, condenses several explanatory passages, repairs blank section references, and integrates the former appendix material into the main narrative.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 3, 4, and 9 are redrawn, and Figures 6-8 receive revised plots and expanded legends. Figure 8 grows from four to six panels, while the Scaffold algorithm and Neurotoxin illustration move into the main text. Table 1's borders and the overall layout are also revised; Figure 5 retains its original visual content.

improvement.justification: The added IBA/3DFed comparisons and FLAME/SparseFed tests improve empirical breadth, and the organization is clearer. However, v3 makes benign-client amplification and greater vulnerability than FedAvg central claims without direct comparative or mechanism-isolating tests. The unexplained Figure 6e ranking reversal and the claim of four simultaneous defenses despite Figure 8's separate conditions further complicate assessment. These gains and unresolved evidential problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
